title: 3M's expert told ChatGPT 'show how 3M is 0% at fault' - jury awarded $61M
description:
Fluent AI text is clearing institutional checkpoints faster than verification systems can keep up. A $475/hr expert witness used ChatGPT to write roughly 90% of a court report in the Watson Grinding explosion case, prompting it to show 3M was "0% at fault." The jury awarded more than $61 million and assigned 3M 30% of the blame. In Australia, a $3.5 million government age-check trial included fabricated ChatGPT citations in a report that informed a national social media ban for children under 16. In Washington, AI-generated bill drafts are overwhelming the office that turns lawmakers' intentions into statutory language.
For generations, a polished document signaled that someone had done the work behind it. When producing fluent text costs almost nothing, that signal breaks down, and authority migrates to whoever can show the checking. Every one of these failures was eventually caught by opposing counsel, metadata reviewers, or professional drafters. The verification layer is forming through exactly these collisions.
